metadata.title: Event Streaming

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for emitting and consuming high-volume, append-only event streams as authoritative system-to-system signals.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Event streaming platforms supporting high-throughput publication, subscription, partitioning, and fan-out consumption.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern for governing trust, amplification, and semantic stability in event-driven architectures.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Event streaming trust assumes baseline integration identity, ownership, boundary, and accountability guarantees.

metadata.remarks: Event Streaming defines trust properties required for high-volume, fan-out event systems where downstream consumers implicitly trust emitted events. This pattern addresses amplification risk, ordering assumptions, consumer isolation, and event lifecycle without addressing schemas or message authentication.

components.title: Event Producer Authority
components.description: Ensures only authorized systems may emit events on a given stream or topic.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of valid service identities to publish unauthorized events.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Masquerading as a trusted event producer.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Strong non-human identity binding for event producers.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Producer systems emitting events are authenticated.
Enforcement mechanisms prevent unauthorized event publication.

components.title: Fan-Out and Amplification Control
components.description: Constrains uncontrolled amplification of events across multiple downstream consumers.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Manipulation of event flow to trigger disproportionate downstream effects.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Access and subscription control for event consumers.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Consumers subscribing to event streams are explicitly authorized.
Policies define permissible fan-out and consumer scope.

components.title: Event Ordering and Time Assumptions
components.description: Manages assumptions about event ordering, delivery timing, and temporal correctness.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of event delivery timing or ordering assumptions.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Lifecycle and temporal controls to reduce unsafe ordering assumptions.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Event streaming features are constrained to reduce unsafe temporal assumptions.

components.title: Event Stream Lifecycle Governance
components.description: Defines creation, evolution, and decommissioning of event streams.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Persistence through abandoned or undocumented event streams.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Lifecycle management to reduce residual and orphaned event streams.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Policies define ownership and lifecycle of event streams.

components.title: Event Stream Observability
components.description: Provides visibility into event publication, subscription, and consumption.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Suppression of evidence related to event misuse or propagation.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Audit logging and traceability of event flow.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Event publication and consumption activities are logged.
Audit review supports investigation of event-driven behavior.
